crosswalks.label: Data Scientists
crosswalks.rationale: O*NET directly describes Data Scientists, including data transformation, data mining/modeling, machine learning, visualization, interpretation and reporting; AXM still preserves narrower ownership boundaries inside that occupation.

findings.summary: O*NET provides a direct occupational baseline for the package's data preparation, modeling, machine learning, visualization, interpretation and reporting work.
findings.rationale: The candidate body substantially matches the occupational core while separating production/data-engineering/statistical/domain ownership.

findings.summary: Even with an exact occupation match, exploratory/predictive work must not silently become causal/statistical or domain/product decision authority.
method_labels: O*NET occupational baseline plus AXM profession-boundary review
findings.rationale: The occupation spans modeling and interpretation; AXM needs explicit inference/action boundaries for portable professional machinery.

gaps_against_body.description: Make descriptive, exploratory, predictive, causal/statistical and domain/product decision surfaces explicit so model output cannot silently upgrade into stronger claims or authority.

nonclaims: This packet does not claim complete reconstruction of every Data Scientist specialty despite the exact occupation match.
An exact O*NET occupation mapping is human-work baseline evidence, not automatic TEST competence or authority transfer.
No causal, product, domain, production-ML, TEST, WORKING or CANON claim is created.

high_stakes.authorization_nonclaim: This packet grants no statistical, causal, product, domain, production, security, legal or institutional authority.
